title: Robot Arms: Build Ari
tagline: Build a small robot arm, then teach it to pick up a cup.
description: Build a small robot arm: servos, joints, smooth motion, a gentle gripper, calibration and a pick and place job.
outcome: After this course you can plan and build a small robot arm and make it pick up and place an object.
whoFor: Learners who want to build a small robot arm and make it pick up things.
outcomes: Plan a robot arm from a job description
Explain how a servo holds an angle
Count joints and degrees of freedom
Make arm motion smooth, and build a gentle gripper
Calibrate the arm and run a pick and place job

finalActivity.title: Drive, pick and drop
finalActivity.prompt: Describe the drive, pick and drop job you built: list the steps in order, say what can go wrong at each step and how your robot handles it.

lessons.title: The arm box and the plan
lessons.summary: Plan a robot arm: what it must do, and which parts it needs.

quiz.q: What should you decide first when planning a robot arm?
quiz.why: The job decides the reach, strength and parts.

quiz.q: If the arm must pick up a cup, which feature matters?
options: A gripper that opens wide enough
quiz.why: The gripper must fit the cup.

quiz.q: Reach means…
options: How far the arm can extend
quiz.why: Reach is the distance the arm can get to.

quiz.q: Why make a parts list before building?
options: To check you have what the job needs
quiz.why: A list shows missing parts early.

lessons.title: Inside a servo
lessons.summary: Explain what a servo is and how it holds an angle.

quiz.q: What is special about a servo?
options: It can move to and hold an angle
quiz.why: A servo goes to a set angle and holds it.

quiz.q: What lets a servo know its angle?
quiz.why: A sensor reports the shaft position.

quiz.q: A servo is told which angle to go to by…
quiz.why: The control signal sets the target angle.

quiz.q: If a servo is asked to hold an angle and is pushed, it will…
options: Push back to return to the angle
quiz.why: Feedback makes it correct itself.

lessons.title: Joints and degrees of freedom
lessons.summary: Count how many ways an arm can move.

quiz.q: What is a degree of freedom?
options: One independent way a part can move
quiz.why: Each independent motion adds a degree of freedom.

quiz.q: An arm with three joints that each turn has…
quiz.why: Each turning joint adds one.

quiz.q: Why do more degrees of freedom help?
options: The arm can reach more positions
quiz.why: More ways to move means more places it can reach.

quiz.q: What is a downside of too many joints?
options: More to control and more that can go wrong
quiz.why: Extra joints add complexity.

lessons.title: Smooth motion
lessons.summary: Make the arm move gently instead of snapping to a position.

quiz.q: Why is snapping suddenly to a position a problem?
options: It can shake the arm or drop things
quiz.why: Sudden moves cause jerks and drops.

quiz.q: How do you make an arm move smoothly?
options: Move in many small steps toward the target
quiz.why: Small steps spread the move over time.

quiz.q: Slowing down near the end of a move helps because…
options: The arm arrives gently without overshoot
quiz.why: Easing in stops overshoot.

quiz.q: A gentler move is also kinder to…
options: The gears and the object being carried
quiz.why: Smooth motion reduces wear and drops.

lessons.title: The gripper
lessons.summary: Design a gripper that holds a cup without crushing it.

quiz.q: What is the goal of a good gripper?
quiz.why: Enough grip to hold, not enough to damage.

quiz.q: Soft pads on the fingers help because…
options: They grip better and protect the object
quiz.why: Soft pads add friction and cushioning.

quiz.q: How can you stop a gripper crushing a cup?
options: Make it close fully every time
Limit how far or how hard it closes
quiz.why: Limiting the closing stops over-squeezing.

quiz.q: Why test the gripper on the real cup?
options: Real objects behave differently from guesses
quiz.why: Testing on the real thing reveals problems.

lessons.title: Reach and geometry
lessons.summary: Use two links and angles to reach a point.

quiz.q: An arm made of two links is useful because…
options: It is always fixed in place
Changing the angles moves the hand to different points
quiz.why: Two links with angles can reach many positions.

quiz.q: To reach a farther point, the arm should…
quiz.why: Straighter links reach farther.

quiz.q: Angles and link lengths together decide…
quiz.why: Geometry links joint angles to hand position.

quiz.q: If a point is beyond the arm's reach, the arm…
options: Reaches it with a new battery
Cannot reach it however it moves
quiz.why: Reach is limited by link lengths.

lessons.title: Calibration
lessons.summary: Fix small errors so the arm goes where it should.

quiz.q: What does calibration do?
options: Matches the arm's real position to what you ask for
quiz.why: Calibration corrects small errors.

quiz.q: Why can an arm miss its target slightly?
options: Parts are slightly loose or off-centre
quiz.why: Small mechanical errors add up.

quiz.q: A good way to calibrate is to…
options: Move to known positions and adjust until they match
quiz.why: Compare against known spots and adjust.

quiz.q: After calibrating you should…
options: Test again to check the fix
quiz.why: Retesting confirms the improvement.

lessons.title: Pick and place
lessons.summary: Break a job into steps using a simple state machine.

quiz.q: What is a state machine?
options: A list of steps where the robot is in one step at a time
quiz.why: A robot moves from one named step to the next.

quiz.q: A pick job might have steps…
options: Move above, lower, close gripper, lift
quiz.why: Pick is a clear sequence of small actions.

quiz.q: Why split the job into steps?
options: Each step is easy to test and fix
quiz.why: Small steps make debugging easier.

quiz.q: What should happen if a step fails?
options: The robot goes to a safe step or stops
quiz.why: Plan what to do when something goes wrong.

lessons.title: Mounting Ari on Pip
lessons.summary: Join two robots and keep them stable.

quiz.q: What is the main risk when putting an arm on a wheeled robot?
quiz.why: An extended arm shifts the weight.

quiz.q: To keep the robot stable you can…
options: Keep the arm low and the weight central
quiz.why: A low, centred weight resists tipping.

quiz.q: Why check the power supply when joining the robots?
options: Both need enough power to run together
quiz.why: More motors need more power.

quiz.q: Before running the combined robot you should…
options: Test each part alone, then together
quiz.why: Testing step by step finds problems safely.

lessons.title: The first job together
lessons.summary: Combine driving and picking into one job.

quiz.q: A drive, pick and drop job is made of…
quiz.why: Break the job into drive, pick and drop.

quiz.q: Why should the robot stop before picking?
options: It is a rule of physics that robots rest
quiz.why: Standing still gives a steadier pick.

quiz.q: What should you do if the cup is missed?
options: Back up and try again safely
quiz.why: Plan a retry for common failures.

quiz.q: The best sign the job works is…
options: It succeeds several times in a row
quiz.why: Repeatability shows it really works.
